name: Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport
before:
The East Bay's airport, seven miles south of downtown Oakland and twelve miles east of San Francisco, and a genuine alternative for a client staying anywhere on that side of the bay. It is a Southwest Airlines operating base.

The layout works well for connections. There are two terminals and 29 gates, and the two are joined beyond security, so a connecting passenger never has to clear again. International arrivals without pre-clearance are handled in Terminal 1, which is also where Alaska, Delta, Frontier, Hawaiian, Volaris and Viva sit. Terminal 2 is Southwest only.

There are four runways across 2,600 acres, one long commercial runway on the south field and three shorter general aviation runways on the north. Taxiway B joins the two over a bridge across Ron Cowan Parkway. Winds come from the west or north more than 95 per cent of the time, so aircraft almost always arrive from the south east.

Two runways were renumbered in 2013 because the Earth's magnetic field had shifted.
after:
The main airport for the East Bay, seven miles south of downtown Oakland and a genuine alternative for a client staying anywhere on that side of the bay. Southwest Airlines carries the great majority of its passengers.

There are two terminals. Alaska, Delta, Hawaiian and Volaris check in at Terminal 1, and Southwest at Terminal 2.

The airfield covers 2,600 acres, with one long commercial runway on the south field and three shorter general aviation runways on the north.

claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The coordinates check covers only the distance to Oakland, and no second written source was found in two tries (the Port's 2021 fact sheet the article cites is gone, 404; the Port's current pages give no distance).

claims.wasBefore: It is a Southwest Airlines operating base.
claims.why: 'Base' rests on Wikipedia alone within the last twelve months; softened to Southwest carrying the great majority of passengers (BTS, Wikipedia). The San Francisco Chronicle's report on Southwest's pullback at Oakland, which Wikipedia cites, is blocked by this session's egress policy and was not tried another way.

claims.claim: the layout works well for connections; terminals joined beyond security
claims.wasBefore: The layout works well for connections.
claims.why: Rests on the airside link between the terminals, which is Wikipedia alone: the Port's map, FAQ and releases list each terminal's post-security areas separately and never say they connect.

claims.wasBefore: There are two terminals and 29 gates, and the two are joined beyond security, so a connecting passenger never has to clear again
claims.why: The gate count is disputed: Wikipedia 29 (16 and 13), the Port's live map 28 gate labels (Terminal 1 gates 1 to 17, Terminal 2 gates 20 to 32, with no gate 28 shown). The airside link is Wikipedia alone (see above). The two terminals are kept.

claims.wasBefore: International arrivals without pre-clearance are handled in Terminal 1
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the Port's map, FAQ and airline releases do not say where customs is.

claims.wasBefore: which is also where Alaska, Delta, Frontier, Hawaiian, Volaris and Viva sit
claims.why: Viva is no longer on the airport's airline list or terminal map (read 23 Sep 2026), though Wikipedia still lists it. Frontier left Oakland after 2023 and came back on 20 August 2026 (see the held-back note); the map gives no terminal for it. The four airlines the map places in Terminal 1 are kept.
Reworded to what the airport's map says: Southwest checks in at Terminal 2. Wikipedia also has Southwest using Terminal 1 gates.

claims.claim: the name Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport, settled in April 2026
claims.why: Held back: verified, but the old text never gave a name, so this adds a fact. The Port adopted the name in July 2025 and on 28 April 2026 settled San Francisco's trademark lawsuit; the name stays Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport (Port release; Wikipedia adds that 'International' may not be used). The record's Airport Name already matches. Worth a line for agents, since older material says Metropolitan Oakland International.

claims.claim: traffic: 9.2 million in 2025, down about 15 per cent, and still falling in 2026
claims.why: Held back: new facts (the old text gave no traffic figure). The Port counted 9,210,509 passengers in 2025, down 14.74 per cent on 2024's 10,803,382; the FAA's boardings fell 14.36 per cent (4,532,494). January to July 2026 is down another 15.01 per cent on the Port's July report. This is the biggest recent change at Oakland and worth a sentence if Andy agrees.
